title: Any Unitary Gate Can Be Certified Device-Independently In A Quantum Network
authors: Shubhayan Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Shubhayan Sarkar

Device-independent (DI) certification allows the verification of quantum systems based solely on observed statistics, without assumptions about their internal structure. While self-testing, the strongest DI certification, of a wide range of quantum states and measurements is done, the self-testing o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030802] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that any unitary gate can be self-tested device-independently in a quantum network, extending self-testing to all quantum gates.
motivation: Device-independent certification of quantum gates is crucial for secure quantum information processing, but previous self-testing results were limited to specific gates. A general method for certifying arbitrary unitary gates was missing.
method: The author constructs a network scenario where a unitary gate is applied to a shared entangled state, and the resulting correlations are used to self-test the gate via a Bell-type inequality. The proof uses the concept of 'gate robustness' and semidefinite programming.
result: Any unitary gate can be self-tested in a quantum network, with the robustness of the self-testing depending on the gate's properties. The method works for any number of qubits.
conclusion: This result provides a universal framework for device-independent certification of quantum gates, which is essential for building trusted quantum networks and quantum computers.

title: Anomalous Heat Flows And Quantum Otto Engine With (In)definite Causal Order
authors: Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, And Zhong-Xiao Man
abstract:
Author(s): Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, and Zhong-Xiao Man

The principle that heat spontaneously flows from higher temperatures to lower temperatures is a cornerstone of classical thermodynamics. While this principle holds true for macroscopic systems at equilibrium, here we show that, when a quantum system undergoes two thermalization processes in an indef…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030404] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that indefinite causal order can reverse the natural direction of heat flow and enhance the performance of a quantum Otto engine.
motivation: Classical thermodynamics dictates heat flows from hot to cold; the authors explore whether indefinite causal order in quantum processes can violate this principle and improve engine efficiency.
method: They consider a quantum Otto engine where the two thermalization strokes are arranged in an indefinite causal order using a quantum switch, and analyze the resulting heat flows and work output.
result: Indefinite causal order can cause anomalous heat flow from cold to hot and increase the engine's efficiency beyond the standard Otto cycle limit.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order offers a new resource for quantum thermodynamics, enabling counterintuitive heat flows and enhanced performance in quantum thermal machines.

title: Planckian Bound On Quantum Dynamical Entropy
authors: Xiangyu Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Cao

We introduce a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring’s quantum dynamical entropy for quantum systems. It quantifies the amount of information gained about the initial condition from continuously monitoring an observable. A nonzero entropy growth rate can be obtained by monitoring the therm…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030402] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simplified quantum dynamical entropy that quantifies information gain from continuous monitoring, and shows it obeys a Planckian bound.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits on information extraction from quantum systems and connect quantum chaos to thermodynamics.
method: Defines a simplified Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring entropy for quantum systems and analyzes its growth under continuous measurement of an observable.
result: The entropy growth rate is bounded by a Planckian timescale, linking quantum dynamics to thermodynamic bounds.
conclusion: The Planckian bound provides a universal constraint on quantum information dynamics, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and chaos.

title: General Concurrence Percolation On Quantum Networks
authors: Deep Nath And Soumen Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Deep Nath and Soumen Roy

A quantum network is a network of entangled states which can be used to transmit quantum information. Nonmaximally entangled states are not really effective in establishing quantum communication across vast distances. Creating and maintaining a maximally entangled state over which quantum informatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012440] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a general concurrence percolation framework for quantum networks, enabling efficient entanglement distribution using non-maximally entangled states.
motivation: Non-maximally entangled states are ineffective for long-distance quantum communication, but creating maximally entangled states is challenging. The authors aim to develop a percolation-based method to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors propose a general concurrence percolation model on quantum networks, where entanglement is quantified by concurrence, and percolation thresholds are derived for various network topologies.
result: They show that concurrence percolation can achieve a finite percolation threshold even with non-maximally entangled states, enabling robust entanglement distribution across the network.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for using non-maximally entangled states in quantum networks, potentially simplifying experimental implementations and improving scalability.

title: Analytical Construction Of $(n,$ $n−1)$-quantum Random Access Codes Saturating The Conjectured Bound
authors: Takayuki Suzuki
abstract:
Author(s): Takayuki Suzuki

Quantum Random Access Codes (QRACs) embody the fundamental trade-off between the compressibility of information into limited quantum resources and the accessibility of that information, serving as a cornerstone of quantum communication and computation. In particular, the [MATH]-QRACs, which encod…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012441] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically constructs (n, n-1)-quantum random access codes that saturate the conjectured bound, providing optimal trade-offs between encoding dimension and decoding success.
motivation: Quantum random access codes (QRACs) are fundamental for understanding the trade-off between information compression and accessibility in quantum communication. The (n, n-1)-QRACs are particularly important, but their optimal bounds were only conjectured.
method: The author uses analytical constructions based on mutually unbiased bases and symmetric informationally complete measurements to achieve the conjectured bound for (n, n-1)-QRACs.
result: The constructed QRACs achieve the optimal success probability conjectured in the literature, proving the bound is tight for all n.
conclusion: This work provides a complete characterization of (n, n-1)-QRACs, confirming the optimal trade-off and offering insights into quantum communication protocols.

title: Hybrid Single-ion Atomic-ensemble Node For High-rate Remote Entanglement Generation
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

The authors propose to generate entanglement between trapped ions and broadband photons compatible with ensemble-based memories using spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources. Overcoming the bandwidth mismatch between these systems can provide a hybrid quantum network architecture that combines ensemble-based multiplexed entanglement generation and deterministic ion gates, resulting in a significant speed-up in establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum network node combining trapped ions and atomic ensembles for high-rate remote entanglement generation.
motivation: Overcoming bandwidth mismatch between trapped ions and ensemble-based memories to enable a scalable quantum network architecture.
method: Uses spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources to generate broadband photons that interface trapped ions with ensemble memories, enabling multiplexed entanglement generation.
result: The hybrid architecture significantly speeds up establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers compared to direct ion-photon approaches.
conclusion: This hybrid node design offers a practical path toward high-rate quantum repeaters and long-distance quantum networks.

title: Accelerated Relaxation And Mpemba-like Effect For Operators In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

The quantum Mpemba effect occurs when a quantum system, residing far away from the steady state, relaxes faster than a relatively nearer state. We look for the presence of this highly counterintuitive effect in the relaxation dynamics of the operators within the open quantum system setting. Since th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010601] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the quantum Mpemba effect in the relaxation dynamics of operators in open quantum systems, showing that initial states farther from steady state can relax faster.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive phenomenon where a system farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than a nearer one; its existence in operator relaxation within open quantum systems is explored.
method: The authors analyze the relaxation dynamics of operators using open quantum system formalism, likely employing master equations or spectral analysis to compare relaxation rates for different initial operator states.
result: They demonstrate the presence of the Mpemba-like effect for operators, where certain initial operator configurations lead to accelerated relaxation compared to others.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and relaxation phenomena, with potential implications for controlling quantum systems.

title: Photon-mediated Entanglement Between Spin Qubits Beyond The Dispersive Regime
authors: Andrei I. Nikitchenko And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei I. Nikitchenko and Guido Burkard

Dispersively coupled distant qubits in a shared cavity can become entangled through virtual photon exchange with energy-conserving phase evolution of their quantum states. This interaction can potentially be accelerated by operating on resonance, allowing for the exchange of real photons. In this th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045420] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates photon-mediated entanglement between spin qubits beyond the dispersive regime, enabling faster entanglement generation via real photon exchange.
motivation: Dispersive coupling in cavity-mediated entanglement is slow; operating on resonance could accelerate entanglement but introduces challenges from real photon exchange.
method: The authors theoretically analyze two spin qubits coupled to a common cavity mode, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and entanglement dynamics beyond the dispersive approximation.
result: They show that resonant operation can generate high-fidelity entanglement faster than dispersive schemes, with a trade-off involving photon leakage.
conclusion: Resonant photon-mediated entanglement offers a speedup for spin qubit networks, relevant for quantum networking and distributed quantum computing.

title: Thermodynamic Modes Of A Quasiperiodic Mobility-edge System In A Quantum Otto Cycle
authors: Ao Zhou, Feng Lu, Shujie Cheng, And Gao Xianlong
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Zhou, Feng Lu, Shujie Cheng, and Gao Xianlong

We investigate thermodynamic operation of a quasiperiodic lattice with an exact mobility edge, described by the Biddle–Das Sarma model. We use this model as the working medium of a quantum Otto cycle and map its operating mode as a function of the hopping-range parameter [MATH], the initial and final p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034206] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a quasiperiodic lattice with a mobility edge as the working medium of a quantum Otto cycle, mapping its thermodynamic operating modes.
motivation: To understand how quasiperiodic systems with mobility edges can be used as working media in quantum heat engines, potentially offering new regimes of operation.
method: The authors use the Biddle–Das Sarma model to describe the quasiperiodic lattice and analyze the quantum Otto cycle, varying parameters such as hopping range and initial/final phases to map operating modes.
result: They identify distinct thermodynamic modes (e.g., engine, refrigerator) and show how the mobility edge influences performance.
conclusion: Quasiperiodic systems with mobility edges provide a tunable platform for quantum thermodynamic cycles, with potential advantages in efficiency and control.

title: Work And Heat Exchanged During Sudden Quenches Of Strongly Coupled Quantum Systems
authors: Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, And Nicole Yunger Halpern
abstract:
Author(s): Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, and Nicole Yunger Halpern

The authors examine three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat that have been used for quantum systems coupled strongly to the environment. Their study focuses on quenches, processes in which the Hamiltonian changes abruptly. In these processes, the first law of thermodynamics holds for each set of definitions by construction. The authors show that only two sets of definitions obey the second law. They illustrate their findings with a model of two coupled spins.

#ClearMotivation #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014133] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper examines three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat for strongly coupled quantum systems undergoing sudden quenches, and shows that only two sets obey the second law.
motivation: Strongly coupled quantum systems lack a universally accepted definition of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat, which is crucial for understanding quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat from the literature, apply them to sudden quenches, and test compliance with the first and second laws of thermodynamics using a two-spin model.
result: All three definitions satisfy the first law by construction, but only two of them obey the second law, highlighting the importance of choosing appropriate definitions for strongly coupled systems.
conclusion: The study provides guidance on selecting consistent thermodynamic definitions for strongly coupled quantum systems, advancing the foundation of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Unified Speed Limits In Classical And Quantum Dynamics Via Temporal Fisher Information
authors: Tomohiro Nishiyama And Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Nishiyama and Yoshihiko Hasegawa

The importance of Fisher information is increasing in nonequilibrium thermodynamics, as it has played a fundamental role in trade-off relations such as thermodynamic uncertainty relations and speed limits. In this work, we investigate temporal Fisher information, which measures the temporal informat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014120] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper unifies classical and quantum speed limits using temporal Fisher information, establishing a fundamental trade-off between the rate of change of a system and the Fisher information about time.
motivation: Speed limits are crucial in thermodynamics and quantum information, but a unified framework for classical and quantum systems was lacking. The authors aim to derive a general bound using Fisher information.
method: The authors define temporal Fisher information for both classical and quantum dynamics and prove that the speed of state change is bounded by the square root of the Fisher information. They apply this to various systems, including Markovian and unitary dynamics.
result: They obtain a unified speed limit that recovers known classical and quantum bounds, and show that the Fisher information provides a tighter bound than previous measures like the Wigner-Yanase skew information.
conclusion: Temporal Fisher information offers a universal tool for deriving speed limits, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Detecting Strongly non-Gaussian Entanglement
authors: Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, And Nicolas J. Cerf
abstract:
Author(s): Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, and Nicolas J. Cerf

Efficiently certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable quantum systems is a central challenge for advancing quantum information processing, photonic quantum computing, and metrology. Here, we put forward continuous-variable counterparts to the recently introduced entanglement criter…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes continuous-variable entanglement criteria to detect strongly non-Gaussian entanglement using higher-order moments.
motivation: Certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable systems is crucial for quantum information processing but remains challenging due to the complexity of non-Gaussian states.
method: Derives entanglement criteria based on higher-order moments of quadrature operators, extending recent discrete-variable criteria to the continuous-variable setting.
result: The criteria can detect entanglement in states that evade Gaussian entanglement criteria, including photon-subtracted squeezed states and cat states.
conclusion: The proposed criteria provide an efficient tool for certifying non-Gaussian entanglement, advancing quantum information with continuous variables.

title: Single- And Double-click High-rate Entanglement Generation Between Distant Ions Using Multiplexed Atomic Ensembles
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

In an accompanying paper [B. Tissot et al.,
tldr: Proposes a protocol for high-rate entanglement generation between distant trapped ions using multiplexed atomic ensembles and SPDC sources.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks by efficiently entangling remote ion-based quantum processors via ensemble-based quantum memories.
method: Uses spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) sources interfaced with trapped ions and atomic ensembles, employing multiplexing to enhance entanglement generation rates.
result: Demonstrates that single- and double-click protocols achieve high entanglement rates, overcoming limitations of previous approaches.
conclusion: The proposed interface is a promising building block for future quantum networks connecting ion processors.

title: Partially Device-independent Quantum Cryptography In Asymmetric Networks
authors: Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, And Kai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, and Kai Chen

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation between distant users, yet its standard device-dependent implementations rely on fully characterized and accurately modeled devices. Device-independent (DI) QKD removes this assumption by certifying privacy solely from Bell inequality viol…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033060] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a partially device-independent QKD protocol for asymmetric networks, achieving high key rates with minimal trust assumptions.
motivation: Standard QKD requires fully characterized devices, while fully DI-QKD is impractical due to low key rates. The authors aim to bridge this gap by relaxing trust assumptions only on the more powerful node.
method: They design a protocol where one node is fully characterized and the other is untrusted, using a Bell inequality violation to certify security. Security is proven using the entropy accumulation theorem.
result: The protocol achieves key rates orders of magnitude higher than fully DI-QKD in asymmetric network scenarios, with security against general attacks.
conclusion: Partially device-independent QKD offers a practical trade-off between security and performance, suitable for realistic asymmetric quantum networks.

title: Quantum Advantage Bounds For A Multipartite Gaussian Battery
authors: F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, And M. Sassetti
abstract:
Author(s): F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, and M. Sassetti

We demonstrate the possibility of a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of quantum batteries by analyzing a model that enables a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes. Our system consists of [MATH] harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033045] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of a multipartite Gaussian quantum battery.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but a fair comparison between quantum and classical regimes is needed to confirm genuine quantum advantage.
method: The authors model a system of harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving under a Lindblad master equation, and compare charging efficiency in quantum and classical limits.
result: They find that quantum correlations (entanglement) can enhance charging efficiency beyond classical bounds, establishing a genuine quantum advantage.
conclusion: Quantum batteries can outperform classical ones in charging efficiency, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and energy storage at the quantum scale.

title: Operational Coherent Measurements With Steering And Randomness
authors: Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, And Hsi-Sheng Goan
abstract:
Author(s): Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, and Hsi-Sheng Goan

Measurement incompatibility underpins randomness generation in nonlocal phenomena. However, at its root, a more fundamental quantum feature is noncommuting (or coherent) measurements. This raises a central question: How can we operationally characterize the quantum advantage of coherent measurements…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033054] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper operationally characterizes the quantum advantage of coherent measurements through steering and randomness generation.
motivation: Measurement incompatibility is known to underpin randomness generation, but the fundamental role of coherent (noncommuting) measurements is not fully understood. The authors aim to provide an operational characterization of the quantum advantage of coherent measurements.
method: The authors develop a framework linking coherent measurements to steering and randomness, using semidefinite programming and information-theoretic measures.
result: They show that coherent measurements provide a quantum advantage in steering and randomness generation, quantified by new operational measures.
conclusion: Coherent measurements are a fundamental resource for quantum information tasks, and their operational characterization via steering and randomness offers insights into quantum foundations and applications.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:
Author(s): Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, and Zain H. Saleem

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033040] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved using noisy quantum networks that distribute noisy entangled states, deriving a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information.
motivation: Distributed sensing with quantum networks promises enhanced precision, but noise in entanglement distribution typically degrades performance. The authors aim to show that even with noisy networks, quantum advantage is possible.
method: The authors derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states subject to noise, modeling the network as distributing noisy entangled states.
result: They find that quantum advantage persists for a range of noise levels and network sizes, with the QFI scaling super-classically despite imperfections.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks can still enable quantum-enhanced distributed sensing, motivating practical implementations with current technology.

title: Dispersive Detection Of Single Microwave Photons With Quantum Dots
authors: Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, And Gianluca Rastelli
abstract:
Author(s): Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, and Gianluca Rastelli

Within a circuit quantum electrodynamics architecture, we theoretically investigate the detection of a single propagating microwave photon traveling through a resonant microwave cavity dispersively interacting with a double quantum dot tunnel coupled to a lead. Under suitable conditions, a single ph…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033034] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically proposes a single microwave photon detector using a double quantum dot dispersively coupled to a cavity, enabling high-fidelity detection via charge transport.
motivation: Single microwave photon detection is crucial for quantum information processing and communication, but existing detectors face challenges in efficiency and noise. This work aims to provide a scalable, high-fidelity detection scheme.
method: The authors model a circuit QED setup where a double quantum dot is tunnel-coupled to a lead and dispersively interacts with a microwave cavity. They analyze the system's dynamics using master equations and input-output theory to compute detection efficiency and dark count rates.
result: Under optimal conditions, the detector achieves near-unity detection efficiency with low dark count probability, and the detection mechanism is robust against moderate experimental imperfections.
conclusion: The proposed detector offers a promising route for integrating single-photon detection into hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum networks and circuit QED.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing finite-size scaling laws and entanglement dynamics that enhance charging power in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging via collective quantum effects, but the interplay between entanglement and scaling laws in open systems is not fully understood.
method: The authors study N-qubit cavity-coupled quantum batteries under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics using Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, deriving finite-size scaling laws and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption leads to charging power scaling as O(N^2) in the ideal case, with entanglement playing a key role, and that open-system effects modify the scaling exponents.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental insights into quantum battery performance and highlight the importance of entanglement for achieving quantum advantage in energy storage.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active stabilization; existing methods are complex and resource-intensive. The authors aim to achieve stable entanglement autonomously.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two remote qubits are coupled via a common waveguide, and use a squeezed vacuum field to autonomously stabilize the entangled state without active feedback.
result: The technique achieves high-fidelity remote entanglement that is robust against imperfections and decoherence, with stabilization times exceeding the bare coherence times.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization offers a scalable and practical approach for maintaining remote entanglement in quantum networks, advancing the feasibility of distributed quantum computing and communication.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two spatially separated superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust and high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two transmon qubits are coupled to a common microwave resonator that is driven by a squeezed vacuum source, creating a nonlocal squeezed reservoir that mediates stationary entanglement.
result: Stationary entanglement is achieved with a concurrence up to 0.15, and the scheme is robust to qubit frequency fluctuations and decoherence.
conclusion: This autonomous reservoir engineering approach offers a scalable and low-complexity method for distributing entanglement in future quantum networks.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across multiple domains, highlighting a nuanced landscape beyond just computational speedups.
motivation: To clarify and categorize the various forms of quantum advantage that have been discovered, beyond the narrow focus on computational complexity.
method: The authors survey and synthesize results from quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum sensing, and quantum simulation, presenting a unified framework.
result: They identify several distinct types of quantum advantage, including exponential, polynomial, and constant-factor improvements, as well as advantages in precision and security.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is a multifaceted phenomenon; understanding its full scope is crucial for guiding future research and practical applications.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity. Tin-vacancy centers in diamond offer promising optical properties but achieving strong coupling has been challenging.
method: Fabricated high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond and integrated single tin-vacancy centers. Measured cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling using resonance fluorescence and photon correlation techniques.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong spin-photon coupling with high efficiency and low noise.
conclusion: This platform is suitable for high-fidelity entanglement generation and scalable quantum network nodes, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking applications.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, introducing a criterion that separates classical and nonclassical processes.
result: The unified rule recovers standard quantum signatures (e.g., Bell nonlocality) and identifies new nonclassical behaviors in seemingly classical processes.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a tool for generating and maintaining entanglement.
method: They propose a hybrid system where multiple spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity, and by engineering the dissipation (e.g., through cavity loss and drive), they create a dissipative steady state that is entangled. The reconfigurability is achieved by tuning external parameters.
result: The scheme produces steady-state entanglement that is robust against imperfections and can be reconfigured to realize different entangled states, including those useful for sensing beyond the standard quantum limit and for simulating topological phases.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to harnessing dissipation for entanglement generation in hybrid quantum systems, with applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies and mitigates loss mechanisms in high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence time and cooperativity.
motivation: Mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits are promising for quantum information processing, but their performance is limited by loss mechanisms that are not fully understood.
method: The authors optimize piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators and characterize loss channels through systematic experiments and materials analysis.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and provide a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of loss in hybrid quantum systems and offers practical guidelines for building high-coherence mechanical resonators for quantum applications.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, but existing methods have high overhead or require complex connectivity.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy physical Bell pairs and error correction to produce a logical Bell pair with improved fidelity, requiring only 2D local connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly lower spacetime volume compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work enables practical distributed quantum computation by reducing the resource overhead for logical Bell pair generation.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks, efficient and stable photon extraction from atomic qubits is needed.
method: A parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip with fiber coupling is designed and characterized for photon collection from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves high photon extraction efficiency and mechanical stability, suitable for quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This compact node design advances practical quantum network implementations by improving photon collection and system robustness.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information protocols, but existing methods are limited.
method: A complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is developed to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the method is experimentally validated on a trapped-ion platform.
conclusion: This work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for device-independent protocols and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A minimal quantum detector model reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum sensors and autonomous machines.
method: The authors analyze a quantum particle-detector model using nonequilibrium thermodynamics, deriving bounds on entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They demonstrate a trade-off between the accuracy of information acquisition and the entropy produced, providing a thermodynamic cost for quantum measurements.
conclusion: The results offer new insights into the fundamental limits of quantum detectors as autonomous thermodynamic machines.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the physical origins of this instability is essential for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study cavity-coupled erbium ions in silicon, using optical spectroscopy and noise analysis to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify specific sources of spectral instability, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can mitigate some decoherence effects.
conclusion: The findings provide a pathway to stabilize single-photon emitters in silicon, advancing their use in quantum networking and computation.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global microwave pulses and optical heralding to generate and verify large cluster states.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with low overhead, scalable to 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter using solid-state spin ensembles, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking applications.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can enhance the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in monitored quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes, deriving conditions for decodability and characterizing logical measurement statistics using information-theoretic tools.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability, and identify regimes where partial measurements stabilize logical information.
conclusion: Random measurements can be beneficial for quantum error correction, offering new insights into the interplay between monitoring and code performance.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of emitters and time steps required, while maintaining high entanglement distribution rates over lossy channels.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-codes offer a practical path toward near-term quantum repeater implementations with improved performance.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with long coherence time and high-fidelity single-shot readout, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Scalable quantum technologies require solid-state spin qubits with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout. Current platforms like NV centers in diamond face limitations, motivating the search for alternative host materials.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, demonstrating a 4-ms spin coherence time and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The ZnO defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, leading to long coherence and high readout fidelity, making it competitive with leading qubit platforms.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering advantages in material growth and integration.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization parameters, allowing for practical device imperfections.
result: The framework yields rigorous security bounds that account for realistic device behavior, enabling standards and certification.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, providing a path to certified QKD devices with provable security.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity flips, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure errors.
result: The erasure conversion leads to a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to error suppression in superconducting quantum processors by exploiting erasure conversion.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable quantum communication, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in metropolitan distances.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, discrete modulation, and measurement-device-independent variants), security proofs (finite-size, composable, and asymptotic), and experimental implementations.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and rates, with security proofs maturing to cover realistic imperfections; the field is now moving toward network demonstrations and integration with quantum repeaters.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and rapidly advancing field, with strong potential for practical quantum networks.

title: Experimental Evidence For Strong Emergent Correlations Between Particles In A Switching Trap
authors: Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, And Grégory Schehr
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, and Grégory Schehr

We experimentally study a system of [MATH] two-dimensional Brownian particles, each confined in a harmonic trap with identical stiffness. The stiffness switches simultaneously between two values at random Poissonian times. This collective switching drives the system into a nonequilibrium stationary s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of Brownian particles in a switching trap reveals strong emergent correlations in a nonequilibrium steady state.
motivation: To understand how collective switching drives correlations in many-particle systems out of equilibrium.
method: Trajectories of Brownian particles in a harmonic trap with randomly switching stiffness are recorded and analyzed.
result: Strong emergent correlations between particles are observed, characterized by a correlation length that diverges as the switching rate decreases.
conclusion: The system provides a tunable platform to study nonequilibrium correlations and collective behavior in stochastic systems.

title: Inverse Clausius Thermodynamics In Run-and-Tumble Dynamics
authors: Oded Farago
abstract:
Author(s): Oded Farago

We establish a mapping between one-dimensional run-and-tumble particle dynamics in the presence of thermal noise, and overdamped Brownian motion in a spatially inhomogeneous temperature field. The approach is formulated as an inverse-Clausius thermodynamic framework, where the effective temperature …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a mapping between run-and-tumble particle dynamics and Brownian motion in inhomogeneous temperature, formulating an inverse-Clausius thermodynamic framework.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic behavior of active matter systems, specifically run-and-tumble particles, which are a model for bacterial motion.
method: Derives an effective temperature description by mapping the run-and-tumble dynamics to overdamped Brownian motion in a spatially varying temperature field, using an inverse-Clausius approach.
result: The mapping yields an effective temperature that depends on the run length and thermal noise strength, capturing the non-equilibrium steady state properties.
conclusion: The inverse-Clausius framework provides a thermodynamic interpretation of active matter, linking it to equilibrium-like concepts despite being out of equilibrium.

title: Connecting Magic Dynamics In Thermofield Double States To Spectral Form Factors
authors: Ning Sun And Pengfei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ning Sun and Pengfei Zhang

Under unitary evolution, chaotic quantum systems initialized in simple states rapidly develop high complexity, precluding any efficient classical description. The hardness of classical simulation within the stabilizer formalism, commonly referred to as magic resources, can be quantified by the stabi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030401] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper connects magic dynamics in thermofield double states to spectral form factors, providing a new perspective on complexity growth in chaotic quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding the growth of quantum complexity in chaotic systems is fundamental, and magic (non-stabilizerness) is a key resource for hardness of classical simulation.
method: The authors analytically and numerically study the time evolution of magic in thermofield double states under random unitary circuits, relating it to spectral form factors.
result: They find that magic dynamics exhibits a linear growth regime followed by saturation, and the growth rate is connected to the spectral form factor, a diagnostic of chaos.
conclusion: The work establishes a quantitative link between magic and spectral properties, offering a new tool to probe quantum chaos and complexity.

title: Characterizing high-Schmidt-number Witnesses In Arbitrary-dimensional Systems
authors: Liang Xiong And Nung-Sing Sze
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Xiong and Nung-sing Sze

A profound comprehension of quantum entanglement is crucial for the progression of quantum technologies. The degree of entanglement can be assessed by enumerating the entangled degrees of freedom, leading to the determination of a parameter known as the Schmidt number (SN). In this paper, we develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012443] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a method to characterize high-Schmidt-number entanglement witnesses in arbitrary-dimensional systems.
motivation: Understanding the degree of entanglement via Schmidt number is crucial for quantum technologies, but constructing witnesses for high Schmidt numbers is challenging.
method: The authors propose a systematic approach to construct entanglement witnesses that can detect states with a given Schmidt number, using the concept of optimal witnesses and semidefinite programming.
result: They provide explicit examples of witnesses for various dimensions and Schmidt numbers, demonstrating the effectiveness of their method.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of entanglement detection and classification, offering practical tools for quantum information processing.

title: Finite-time Thermal Refrigerator In Interacting Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, And Pablo D. Mininni
abstract:
Author(s): Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, and Pablo D. Mininni

We study a finite-time thermodynamic refrigeration cycle realized numerically in three-dimensional, weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs). The setup consists of three spatially separated condensates (system, piston, and reservoir) coupled through time-dependent potential barriers that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013315] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A finite-time refrigeration cycle using interacting Bose-Einstein condensates is numerically demonstrated, showing cooling of a system below the reservoir temperature.
motivation: To explore quantum thermodynamic cycles in many-body systems and understand the role of interactions and finite-time effects in refrigeration.
method: Numerical simulations of three coupled BECs with time-dependent potential barriers, implementing a thermodynamic cycle analogous to a refrigerator.
result: The system BEC is cooled below the reservoir temperature, with performance depending on interaction strength and cycle duration.
conclusion: Interacting BECs can serve as working substances for quantum refrigerators, with finite-time operation and interactions playing key roles.

title: Long-term Stability Of Quantum Resources Through Gravitational Cat States In A Dissipative Markovian Environment
authors: Anas Ait Chlih And Tamer A. Seoudy
abstract:
Author(s): Anas Ait Chlih and Tamer A. Seoudy

The paradigm in which gravity can generate entanglement between distant masses represents a profound shift in our understanding of quantum-gravitational interfaces and is still among the active and debated topics. Recent work [A. ur Rahman et al.,
tldr: This paper investigates the long-term stability of quantum resources (entanglement, discord, coherence) in gravitational cat states under a dissipative Markovian environment.
motivation: Understanding how gravity affects quantum resources is crucial for quantum-gravitational interfaces, but the stability of these resources in realistic noisy environments is unknown.
method: The authors model a gravitational cat state interacting with a Markovian reservoir and compute the dynamics of entanglement, discord, and coherence using standard measures.
result: They find that certain quantum resources can persist for long times despite dissipation, with gravitational coupling providing a stabilizing effect.
conclusion: Gravitational cat states may serve as robust quantum resources for quantum information tasks, even in the presence of environmental noise.

title: Precision-induced Irreversibility In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, And Diego Bautista Avilés
abstract:
Author(s): Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, and Diego Bautista Avilés

Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, yet finite dynamic range imposes a sharp operational limit on reversibility. We identify precision-induced irreversibility: Amplification, mode mixing (as warranted by non-normality), and a finite resolution floor—whether set by detector noise, e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012207] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies precision-induced irreversibility in non-Hermitian systems due to finite dynamic range, linking amplification and mode mixing to operational irreversibility.
motivation: Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, but practical limitations like finite resolution and noise impose a fundamental limit on reversibility, which has implications for information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze non-Hermitian systems with amplification and non-normality, incorporating a finite resolution floor to model operational constraints, and derive conditions for irreversibility.
result: They show that precision-induced irreversibility arises from the interplay of amplification, mode mixing, and finite dynamic range, providing a quantitative measure of irreversibility.
conclusion: This work bridges non-Hermitian physics and thermodynamics, highlighting fundamental limits on reversibility in quantum systems with practical implications for information processing.

title: Detection Of Mpemba Effect Through Observables In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

The quantum Mpemba effect refers to the anomalous relaxation of a quantum state that, despite being initially farther from the steady state, relaxes faster than a closer counterpart. Detecting such a quantum Mpemba effect typically requires full knowledge of the quantum state during its time evoluti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014311] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to detect the quantum Mpemba effect using only observable quantities, without full state tomography.
motivation: Detecting the quantum Mpemba effect typically requires full knowledge of the quantum state, which is experimentally demanding. The authors aim to provide a simpler detection method based on observables.
method: The authors derive conditions for the Mpemba effect in open quantum systems using the time evolution of expectation values of observables, and illustrate with examples of qubit and harmonic oscillator systems.
result: They show that the Mpemba effect can be detected by monitoring a single observable, such as energy or magnetization, and provide criteria based on the observable's relaxation rate.
conclusion: The work offers a practical tool for experimental observation of the quantum Mpemba effect, advancing the understanding of anomalous relaxation in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Restoring Detailed Balance In non-Hermitian Markov Processes
authors: Tim van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, And Christophe Deroulers
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, and Christophe Deroulers

Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often involve asymmetric contributions that break detailed balance and lead to nonmonotonic entropy production, limiting thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques. Here we use Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in those processes, allo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014131] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in non-Hermitian Markov processes, enabling thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques.
motivation: Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often break detailed balance, leading to nonmonotonic entropy production that limits thermodynamic interpretations and inference.
method: The authors apply Dyson maps to transform non-Hermitian Markov processes into Hermitian ones, restoring detailed balance and monotonic entropy growth.
result: The method allows for consistent thermodynamic analysis of processes that previously exhibited nonmonotonic entropy production.
conclusion: Restoring detailed balance via Dyson maps broadens the applicability of thermodynamic concepts to a wider class of stochastic processes.

title: Stroboscopic Saturation Of Multiparameter Quantum Limits In Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: Berihu Teklu And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Berihu Teklu and Victor Montenegro

A naturally multiparameter sensing scenario arises in spatially distributed networks of quantum sensors, where each node probes a distinct parameter of interest. In such settings, the central challenges are to achieve quantum-enhanced sensitivity under well-defined resource constraints and to explic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033053] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies multiparameter quantum sensing in distributed networks, deriving fundamental limits and showing that stroboscopic control can saturate the quantum limits.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing networks face challenges in achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity under resource constraints. Understanding the fundamental limits and how to saturate them is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for multiparameter estimation in a network of quantum sensors, using quantum Fisher information matrix and considering stroboscopic control to optimize the sensing protocol.
result: They derive the multiparameter quantum limits and demonstrate that stroboscopic control allows saturating these limits, providing a clear advantage over static protocols.
conclusion: Stroboscopic control is an effective strategy to achieve optimal sensitivity in distributed quantum sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and network-based sensing.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven using continuous drives, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive methods could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors design a bosonic code that corrects photon loss errors using continuous drives without active measurements, and experimentally demonstrate it in a superconducting cavity.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, meaning the error-corrected qubit lives longer than the best unprotected qubit in the same system.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can reach breakeven, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, leveraging the high-dimensional Hilbert space of nuclear qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated and transferred between nuclear qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is a promising approach for realizing quantum repeaters and quantum networks with enhanced capacity using defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function negativity. They derive bounds and properties using symplectic geometry and quantum information theory.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, additive under tensor products, and to upper bound the Wigner negativity. It also determines the minimal number of squeezed states required for state preparation and the optimal compression rate.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a powerful and operationally meaningful resource theory for non-Gaussianity, with applications to quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging, especially in finite magnetic fields.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve state-selective, low-loss imaging and loading of atoms in an optical tweezer array, leveraging a three-level lambda system.
result: They achieve high-fidelity (>99%) nondestructive imaging and efficient loading of atom arrays, with reduced scattering and heating compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provide a practical route to scalable neutral-atom quantum information processing, particularly for platforms requiring operation in finite magnetic fields.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding how long-range interactions and kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena, such as quantum scars and blockaded ferromagnetism.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, incorporating kinetically constrained long-range interactions, and analyze its dynamics using analytical and numerical methods.
result: The model predicts blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating how kinetic constraints stabilize these phenomena.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays provide a versatile platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum many-body physics, with potential applications in quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.
